title: ops-sync-weekly-briefing-scratch-2026-05-20
agenda: Quick SLO snapshot and red flags
notes:
High-level: quick personal scratchpad for the weekly SRE ops sync. Use for talking points and action capture. Keep items concise.

Opening: start with 90s SLO summary, then jump to paging trend that Jordan flagged. Call out any immediate customer-impacting regressions.

Tone reminders: this is operational, focus on mitigations first, postmortems later. Capture experiments rather than air-gapped ideas.

Context before meeting: infra rolled out runtime v1.18 two weeks ago; small canary then broad rollout on 2026-05-12. Since then, we've seen intermittent increases in p99 latency on hosted-api routes for long-context requests (>4k tokens). Also more frequent post-deploy pages for DB connection pool exhaustion tied to embedder batching.

Quick checklist to read aloud:
- SLOs live view open on console (bring P99 heatmap)
- Pager graph (last 28 days) pinned
- Post-deploy incident cluster list pulled (INC IDs below)

Useful links to paste into chat during sync: Confluence DB postmortem, INF-1024, runtime PR 708.
slos_snapshot:
Request latency (hosted-api): target P99 <= 200ms; current window P99 = 260ms (rolling 7d). Estimated error budget burn for latency SLO: ~45% last 7d.
Availability SLO (hosted-api): target 99.95%; current 99.92% over 30d (approx 0.03% below target). Remaining error budget: ~30%.
Embedding throughput SLO (dedicated): target 99.9%; currently 99.97% (within budget).
Notes: the latency SLO drift is the primary red flag. Need to confirm whether P99 spikes correlate with specific model families or request shapes (longer contexts, function-calls).
paging_trends:
Observation: pages to oncall increased from avg 12/wk (March-April) to 28 last week. Largest contributors: DB connection pool exhaustion (9 pages), GPU OOMs during heavy quantized model runs (6 pages), and transient 5xx errors from a misrouted fallback (4 pages).
Pattern: 60% of pages happen within 30 minutes after a scheduled deploy or autoscaler event. Hypothesis: sudden concurrency spikes are causing connection pool bursts and KV-cache churn.
Implication: urgent need for deploy-time throttles and more conservative autoscaler thresholds for certain routes. Also consider per-customer connection pooling for heavy embedder tenants.
incidents_summary:
INC-2026-045: DB pool exhaustion on 2026-05-13 after broad rollout of v1.18. Impact: degraded embedding creation and sporadic 5xx for dedicated customers. Root cause suspected: increased batch size + retry amplification. Owner: Samir.
INC-2026-047: GPU OOM flurry on 2026-05-15 during overnight ingestion job; multiple containers restarted, triggered oncall twice. Impact: brief latency spikes for heavy-context endpoints. Root cause suspected: unbounded banner job on staging leaking into prod queue; mitigated by scaling down job. Owner: Priya.
INC-2026-052: Fallback routing misconfiguration on 2026-05-18; requests routed to CPU-only variant causing 5xx/timeouts under load. Impact: visible customer errors for <1 hour. Root cause: rollout flag mismatch between router and model catalog. Owner: Jordan.
root_cause_hypotheses:
1) Tokenizer cache fragmentation in runtime causing memory spikes under long-context requests -> leads to more GC/eviction and higher tail latency. Test: enable verbose mem metrics on canary with long-context synthetic traffic.
2) Embedding batch size auto-tuner increases batch size aggressively under certain latency signals, amplifying DB connection usage and triggering pool exhaustion. Test: freeze batch size to baseline and monitor.
3) Rollout orchestration race where router health checks lag model catalog updates -> temporary mismatch (cpu vs gpu). Test: add pre-rollout validation step to compare router routes vs catalog versions.

Short sync: Samir & Maya 2026-05-21 9:30am PT to confirm alert thresholds rolled out.
Postmortem owners to convene after each incident stabilizes; template check: include latency graphs, deploy timeline, and mitigation timeline.
Consider a one-week pause on non-critical broad rollouts for runtime v1.18 until mitigations validated (decision due 2026-05-23).
retrospective_notes:
What worked: quick hotfix for routing mismatch reduced customer impact; oncall response timeline within SLA.
What didn't: rollout automation did not catch catalog-router parity; autoscaler thresholds too aggressive for bursty embedder patterns.
Experiment items: run canaries with synthetic workload that mimics busiest tenant profiles; explore connection pool sharding per tenant for heavy embed cases.
Open question: do we need an SLO change or better customer-level SLAs for large embed workloads? Capture for next product-SRE sync.
